artworks.title: The Cumaean Sibyl (Sistine Chapel)
artworks.description: Michelangelo's monumental prophetess on the Sistine vault — massive limbs and an open book, the Cumaean Sibyl as Renaissance theology's pagan witness to the Word.

artworks.title: Cumaean Sibyl
artworks.description: Domenichino's Capitoline canvas: the Sibyl as a young woman with scroll and laurel — Bolognese clarity for Virgil's guide through the underworld.

artworks.title: Aeneas and the Sibyl in the Underworld
artworks.description: Brueghel's Met panel crowds Aeneas and the Cumaean Sibyl through a hellscape of monsters and fire — Aeneid VI as Flemish cabinet drama.

artworks.title: The Bay of Baiae, with Apollo and the Sibyl
artworks.description: Turner's Tate canvas: Apollo offers the Sibyl as many years as the sand in her hand — the Bay of Baiae dissolving into light while her bargain with immortality fails.

artworks.title: Aeneas and the Sibyl in the Underworld
artworks.description: Burne-Jones' Fitzwilliam design: the Sibyl leads Aeneas among the shades — Pre-Raphaelite stillness for Virgil's most famous katabasis.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Book VI — the golden bough, the gates of sleep, and the Cumaean Sibyl as Aeneas' guide through the underworld.

popCulture.title: The Waste Land
popCulture.creator: T. S. Eliot
popCulture.description: Eliot's epigraph quotes Petronius' Cumaean Sibyl hanging in a jar, wishing only to die — the atlas's most famous modern echo of her failed immortality.

popCulture.title: Cumaean Sibyl
popCulture.description: Apollo's prophetess at Cumae — Virgil's guide, Michelangelo's giantess, Eliot's hanging Sibyl.
